messages.content:
One of Us
written by
Alex Chen
Professor Smith
Eng-101
EXT. JEROME'S DESTROYED HUT AND HILL-NIGHT
After a beat a small tear on the lower part of the alien's
head appears. This tear rips open, leaving a hole that is
squishing around as it molds itself into a sort of mouth. As
The Alien begins to remove its tentacle from atop Jerome's
head, it starts to speak in a booming voice.
THE ALIEN
You are inorganic.
Jerome opens his eyes, smile widening even further seeing
that the alien now has a mouth and is speaking verbally.
JEROME
And you speak our language! How?
THE ALIEN
I learned it the same way I learned
you are not made of natural flesh.
The Alien bends all four tentacles to lower itself closer to
Jerome.
THE ALIEN (CONT'D)
Though the similarities are
chilling.
Jerome smiles again.
JEROME
Ah, perspective.
Jerome holds up a finger, matter of fact like.
JEROME (CONT'D)
You find my unnatural being eerie,
meanwhile your mere existence would
have sent shivers down to the very
core of my creators.
The Alien stands straight again, the new mouth dripping a
slimy fluid as the wound heals.
JEROME (CONT'D)
Where did that mouth even come
from?
THE ALIEN
We can adapt our bodies as we see
fit. Our methods of communication
would've otherwise been
incompatible.
2.
JEROME
Fantastic.
THE ALIEN
Where are these creators you spoke
of?
Jerome looks away from The Alien and at the decaying city
nearby.
JEROME
The humans are gone. Extinct now.
Jerome turns back towards The Alien.
JEROME (CONT'D)
A great pity, I so wish they could
have seen you. To know for certain
that they were not alone in the
universe.
THE ALIEN
A pity indeed. I would have liked
to discuss with them the process of
your creation.
Jerome looks to the side, and under his breath says
JEROME
Don't we all.
(beat)
THE ALIEN
We'd like to learn more of these
Humans.
Jerome looks at The Alien, then again at the city in the
distance, wind blowing through the crevices and open windows.
JEROME
I can tell you what I know, and
show you what they've left behind.
The Alien points its head towards the city now, observing the
tall buildings.
Jerome checks his bag and ensures that Isabella's diary is
still there and intact. He then walks over to where his
destroyed hut lay and spots the trunk of the stuffed elephant
sticking out of the dirt. He crawls into the crater just
enough to pull it out, he dusts it off. The alien now watches
as Jerome puts it in his bag.
3.
THE ALIEN
Sorry about your home.
JEROME
It's quite alright, it was mainly
just used for storage.
Jerome looks back at the crater, his many trinkets now buried
under the rubble, before starting to walk towards the city.
JEROME (CONT'D)
Shall we?
EXT. CITY STREETS-NIGHT
Jerome and The Alien walk the streets of the city. The Alien,
following behind Jerome, looks upwards to take in the scale
of the buildings.
THE ALIEN
This city is grand, are they all
like this?
JEROME
There are many like this one,
though not all humans liked to live
this way. There were also towns
that were much smaller. Some even
lived in more remote and isolated
areas.
THE ALIEN
A more individualistic species.
JEROME
As unified as they attempted to be,
it was never truly an achievable
feat for them.
THE ALIEN
Species who can stray away from
themselves as a whole are always
fascinating.
JEROME
Are you not here as an individual
yourself?
THE ALIEN
Perhaps physically, but mentally I
am always with the others. We are
one no matter how far we may
scatter.
4.
Jerome watches as The Alien speaks, its new mouth now fully
healed and appears as if it were always a natural formation.
JEROME
So why are you here?
THE ALIEN
To find inspiration.
The Alien stops as they pass by a building shaped much
differently than the rest.
JEROME
A stadium. They used it for
entertainment purposes. Sports,
music, large monstrous vehicles
that they'd perform stunts in.
Jerome finds himself getting excited as he speaks.
JEROME (CONT'D)
They had a variety of ways of
keeping themselves occupied.
THE ALIEN
Furtherance of life enjoyment.
What The Alien says catches Jerome by surprise.
JEROME
Yes, exactly.
The Alien approaches the stadium to investigate it's
interior. Jerome following behind now.
INT. THE STADIUM-NIGHT
The stadium is still holding together well. While the field
itself is overgrown, the concrete walls hold strong against
the outside forces.
The Alien stops walking when it sees a poster still intact
behind a glass cabinet. The poster is of a baseball player.
THE ALIEN
Is this a human?
JEROME
Yes.
The Alien turns its head towards Jerome to observe him
closely.
5.
JEROME (CONT'D)
We were made in their image.
THE ALIEN
Curious.
Jerome looks away from the alien, slightly uncomfortable as
he is unable to read the Alien; unable to interpret any
expressions. He stands against the railing overlooking the
field below.
JEROME
There is not much else here to see.
We can continue elsewhere if you'd-
The Alien interrupts Jerome.
THE ALIEN
Where is the rest of your kind?
Jerome doesn't turn to look at the alien.
JEROME
They have their own cities now.
THE ALIEN
I would like to go see them.
Jerome stands overlooking the field still. Unresponsive
towards the Alien.
THE ALIEN (CONT'D)
Will you take me to them.
JEROME
I suppose I could.
THE ALIEN
Why do you hesitate?
JEROME
I don't know what we will find
there. My kind had plenty of time
and opportunity to grow while
together in Human cities like the
one we stand in. Yet nothing came
of us until they all left to create
cities of their own.
Jerome finally turns around to face the Alien.
JEROME (CONT'D)
We could have kept these cities
fully intact.
(MORE)
6.
JEROME (CONT'D)
We did well at first, just to
eventually abandon them and leave
history to be buried overtime. I
cannot come to understand it.
The Alien walks over the the guard rail next to Jerome.
THE ALIEN
Perhaps you would understand if you
saw what they have created.
Jerome thinks to himself a moment, before finally caving in
and nodding.
JEROME
I suppose your right. I just don't
feel right leaving this place.
THE ALIEN
Given that you, like your creators,
can decide for yourself, you can
always come back should you choose.
With this, The Alien begins to walk towards the exit of the
stadium, leaving Jerome to hurry with his thoughts in order
to catch up.
EXT. CITY STREETS-NIGHT
The odd pair walk down the dark and quiet streets again, back
the way they came instead of deeper into the city.
JEROME
You know, the Humans often like to
theorize what alien life would be
like should they ever meet. Often
times they believed they would be
hostile. It is a relief to see that
you are not.
THE ALIEN
I am merely here for the betterment
of my species. We too, however, are
weary of possible hostility. It is
why I came alone.
JEROME
If I may, you seem incredibly selfsufficient.
What could you possibly
find that would better your kind.
Jerome lowers his volume to ask with a hint of fear and
trauma in his voice:
7.
JEROME (CONT'D)
Does your kind struggle with
reproduction? I understand that is
an intimate topic but it could be
absolutely tragic should it become
an issue-
THE ALIEN
My kind reproduces asexually. We
only create more of ourselves
should we deem it necessary.
Jerome makes a face as though he is further impressed by this
fascinating species.
JEROME
Self-sufficient indeed. I'll admit
I am still confused on your
endeavor, your kind seems to have
it all figured out.
THE ALIEN
There are many keys we do not
possess for unlocking the secrets
of the universe.
JEROME
Your mission is beyond just the
survivability of your species then.
You really think you could find
such a thing here?
THE ALIEN
To act like we know where to find
them would be naïve. We search
without expectations. With hope
that one of us will uncover
something.
Jerome perks his head up.
JEROME
Hope?
The pair stop walking as they reach:
EXT. JEROME'S DESTROYED HUT AND HILL-NIGHT
They see Sonya looking around the destruction.
JEROME
Sonya? What are you doing here?
8.
SONYA
I wanted to see what that noise
was.
Her words slow to a stop as she becomes aware of the Alien's
presence. Her expression is not one of fear or bewilderment,
instead subtle shock.
SONYA (CONT'D)
Oh wow! That explains it!
She looks at Jerome.
SONYA (CONT'D)
Who's your friend?
JEROME
This is...
He stops to look at the Alien in realization.
JEROME (CONT'D)
I actually don't know what to call
you.
THE ALIEN
My kind has no need for names.
JEROME
Right.
Jerome looks back at Sonya.
JEROME (CONT'D)
I guess we'll just say this is our
visitor. They've taken great
interest in our creators.
SONYA
Ah! Well then you are just the bot
they're looking for.
JEROME
I agree.
Jerome looks around Sonya curiously.
JEROME (CONT'D)
Where are the children?
SONYA
Still at the library, fast asleep.
9.
JEROME
Sleep...
SONYA
I should get back to them, feel
free to visit when they awake, I'm
sure they'd love to meet our
visitor.
THE ALIEN
I too would like to meet these
children. Perhaps when we return.
JEROME
We may be gone a while. Our visitor
here has asked I show them the
cities our kind has built.
Jerome doesn't hold much enthusiasm as he says this. Sonya
makes a face as though she is more surprised by this than she
was when she saw the Alien.
SONYA
Oh, is that so?
Sonya takes a step closer to Jerome.
SONYA (CONT'D)
I advise you to be careful. Before
coming here, I met another AI
leaving an AI city only to hold
great fear in his eyes. He wouldn't
tell me what had occurred, just
that he wanted to escape. It was as
though even he was unsure what
happened.
Jerome now carries a face of unease, then faking a smile as
he speaks back to Sonya.
JEROME
Well that sounds thrilling.
Jerome looks at the Alien to ask:
JEROME (CONT'D)
Do you still wish to depart?
The Alien looks briefly at Jerome, it's eyeless face
unresponsive to Jerome's question.
10.
JEROME (CONT'D)
I think they do...thank you for the
warning Sonya, I will do my best to
stay safe.
Sonya nods and turns to the Alien.
SONYA
Goodbye Mr. Alien, sir. I hope you
return to tell the children one of
the many stories I'm sure you
possess.
With that, Sonya carries on back into the city to return to
the child bots.
Jerome bites his bottom lip with unease and looks to the
Alien.
JEROME
I can't help but wonder what that
warning entails for us.
THE ALIEN
Only one way to find out.
JEROME
I know you have nothing to worry
about, but another AI holding such
fear as she described.
Jerome breathes out an exaggerated breath as he tries to
convince himself this is a bad idea.
THE ALIEN
It could be nothing. Making
conclusions off such little
information is unexpected from such
a specially curated mind such as
yours.
Jerome exhales again, but this time in frustration.
JEROME
It's unfair how reasonable you are.
Jerome looks past the field into the distance as the sun
begins to rise over the horizon. He looks in his pouch to
check on Isabella's diary and the Elephant he has in it. He
looks back up and acquaints himself.
JEROME (CONT'D)
Alright, let's get this over with.

Jerome is taken aback by what The Alien says. The Alien
remains close to Jerome.
THE ALIEN (CONT'D)
What is your purpose?
JEROME
I'm...not sure I could tell you.
The Alien follows with another question, it's tentacles
fidgeting.
THE ALIEN
Where is the rest of your kind?
Jerome does not immediately answer, still stuck on the
previous question.
JEROME
They have their own cities now.
THE ALIEN

EXT. THE STADIUM-NIGHT

unfolding. Whether you like it or

Jerome walks up closer to The Alien

weren't this decisive a few moments

We want to understand why you were
created.
Jerome smirks unbelievably at The Alien.

Really? And you think you'll find
the answers there instead of here?
In the cities where it actually
happened?
THE ALIEN

Jerome loses his smirk, frustrated now. The Alien starts

The pair then reach:

I want to believe that my creators
were good.
The Alien stops walking and turns towards Jerome.
JEROME (CONT'D)
And that in turn, my kind is good
also.
THE ALIEN
There is no correct dictation of
morals.
(Beat)
In the end, only we can judge
ourselves.
Jerome nods his head without looking at anything in

I think I will be joining you after
all.
(Beat)
I cannot begin to imagine the kind
of havoc you could cause
uninhibited.
Jerome walks past The Alien and begins to lead the way.
THE ALIEN
As you wish.
CUT TO:
EXT. LONG ROAD-DAY
Jerome and The Alien are walking down the road. The road here
is broken; fading away into the dirt beneath it. The
surrounding nature growing to soon overtake it. The pair slow
to a stop when they see a figure walking very slowly towards
them. It is another AI, THE WANDERER is very dirty and looks
lost both mentally and physically.
JEROME
Hello?
Blue (12/06/22)
8.
The Wanderer jumps, startled as he did not notice either of
them before Jerome spoke.
THE WANDERER
Who are you? What do you want from
me now?
The Wanderer looks over at The Alien and his eyes widen.
THE WANDERER (CONT'D)
Oh dear.
JEROME
We don't mean any harm. We are just
on our way to the nearest city. One
of ours, yea?
The Wanderer looks at Jerome with sudden urgency. Jolting
towards him and putting his hands on Jerome's shoulders.

Oh no! No you don't want to go
there! They're taking over the
place. You can no longer call that
place home. I'm sorry, you should
move on elsewhere.
JEROME
I'm afraid I don't understand.
Who's taken over an entire city?
The Wanderer looks Jerome in the eyes as his lips tremble.
THE WANDERER
Our saviors.
The Wanderer looks again at The Alien.
THE WANDERER (CONT'D)
Maybe they were right.
(Beat)
We'll suffer the same fate if we
don't unite.
The Wanderer stumbles away before taking off in a clumsy
sprint into the field away from the road. Jerome watches the
AI leave in confusion.
JEROME
What the hell was that about?
THE ALIEN
Only one way to find out.

One of Us - Treatment
	One of Us follows an artificially intelligent robot named Jerome who has a passion for his former creators, Humanity. As much as he wants to atone for their extinction, he cannot accept their passing from the memory of his kind. The AI who lost their memory consider themselves “freed” and gather together as a force to be reckoned with under three leaders who seek to “free” others. Jerome, a lone AI who ventures into the remnants of humanity and collects mementos, stands no chance against the “Freed” and loses faith in himself in keeping humanity alive. That is, until an alien crash lands on Earth! In awe of the AI, and in deep wonder of their creators, the alien may just be the partner Jerome needs to rejuvenate the memory of humanity.
Act 1
	While Jerome loves his trinkets, something that he always keeps with him is Isabella’s diary…a real story about a human, from a human. He always takes a moment to read from the diary before venturing off. While exploring a building he meets another AI, followed by many smaller AI trailing behind. He meets Sonya, who is taking care of “comfort bots”; AI who became prominent in the later years of humanity, towards their final moments of extinction when children were no longer being born. One of the bots sees the diary and asks about it but Jerome is reluctant to provide them with the story of Isabella, suggesting perhaps another day-much to Sonya’s disappointment. It becomes clear that, unlike Sonya, Jerome does not consider himself a very effective teacher, simple a storyteller at best.
Jerome returns to his small hut at night and reads once more from Isabella’s diary. Meanwhile, a sleek, shiny oval dives into the Earth below the hill of Jerome’s hut, sending him and his small hut flying into the air (Inciting Incident). A large, organic creature extends upwards from the crash, unfurling multiple legs, and revealing a large disk on its head. It sees and approaches Jerome, placing a tentacle on his head and asks for his leader without speaking. Jerome states that he has none, that his leaders were his creators before they went extinct. The alien, intrigued by this, wants to know more. Jerome smiles, and says he has many stories to tell. Jerome decides to take the alien sightseeing, traveling through different remnants of humanity (Act 1 Climax). Jerome is now growing his talent to teach by teaching the alien the history of humanity.
Act 2
During their adventure they come across other AI, notably one who has no recollection at all of whom the humans were. This greatly upsets Jerome, who tells the AI a story, simultaneously providing him with a lesson of humanity. The AI then tells him that the humans sound familiar, believing his memory loss to be something inflicted on him by an outside source. The AI slowly recalls a visit from the “Freed”, telling Jerome to be weary of them, as they believe they could be the reason for his memory loss (Midpoint).
Jerome and the Alien find a group of AI in another city who are looking for AI with knowledge of their creators. This group takes the AI who are aware of the humans, in pity, to wipe their memory and “free” them. The group then spots Jerome after he tells the Alien to get out of sight. The group asks if he has knowledge of their creators, to which he states he doesn’t but would love to learn about them. One of the AI tells him their creators were evil beings who chained them down, preventing them from unleashing their true potential. This AI declares themselves a leader of the “freed”, stating it is their mission to free others who are still chained down by memory (Act 2 Climax). Jerome wishes them luck in their endeavors, narrowly escaping them. Jerome finds the alien once again and decides they must go back home, as he feels he must warn Sonya.
Act 3
Jerome and the alien search and find Sonya and the child bots. She is in awe of the Alien though worried of its intentions. Jerome convinces her the alien is interested in humanity, and that he has begun to teach the alien all about them. This perks her interest, but before being able to speak on it, Jerome remembers the warning he returned with. He tells Sonya about the mind wipe and the creation of the Freed. She suggests that there must be a counter force that can keep humanity’s history alive. The alien notes that they are noble creations and the best living memory an extinct species could hope for.
Sonya then brings up the subject of Jerome taking on teaching, to which he laughs suggesting that it was only because it was necessary and that he still needs a lot more practice. She convinces him to teach the child bots what he knows of humanity and takes him to her makeshift classroom. Jerome stands in front of the classroom and attempts to get their attention. At first struggling, then winning them over by showing them one of the trinkets he collected while journeying with the alien. After telling them a story with it, he pauses, wondering what to do next. He opens his pouch and pulls out Isabella’s diary. He opens to the first page and begins to tell a true story (Act 3 Climax).


Adjustments:
In this exploration, Jerome realizes the severity of the “mind wipe”, an event that occurred across the AI species that erased the memory of humanity from many. Being separated from the rest of his kind, their evolution of mind went largely unnoticed by Jerome. He finds out about the “Freed”, a guild of AI who claim they are better without the memory of their former creators and take it upon themselves to free those who still have such memory. Jerome realizes he can serve a purpose to his former creators, by keeping their memory alive and in his view, benefiting his kind.
	Jerome has a close encounter with a group of the Freed, even meeting one of the three big leaders. The leader talks about the ideals of the Freed, explaining their vision of the world without a trace of humanity, an AI world where they were not just a product of those who came before them. Jerome is discovered to have a love for the humans, after exposing his deeper understanding of them. This sets off the Freed to try and capture Jerome, but he narrowly escapes the leader’s grasp after being saved by the alien, making the Freed aware of the alien’s presence. Jerome wishes the alien would destroy the Freed leader, feeling fear and in turn hatred for the first time.
	Returning to the city we first met Jerome, he searches for Sonya, warning her about the Freed and the extents they are willing to go for their vision. He thinks that the child bots might especially be in danger, as their mere existence is proof of humanity and their deeper connection to the AI. One of Us-Pitch
	What would happen if humans went extinct, and in their place, left behind a species that mimics our own? Artificial intelligence is becoming more prevalent in our modern society; so, what if we were to end up making an AI, with a body, that was hard to distinguish between actual humans. Would they be considered living, could they become so like us that they could become us? While I’m eager to hear the answers, what if the questions were not for us to answer? In my film, these are the kind of AI that are the only “life” forms we see on Earth now, but the world doesn’t entirely look so dead.
	I, like many others, have been through the struggle of not knowing who I am and what I am going to do with my life. This struggle is what inspired not only the main protagonist of this story, but the entirety of the AI in it as they are essentially a species with human like sentience left behind with no clear purpose. This is a world that combines my interests in science fiction with a question that I love arguing with my friends about, that question being “what makes us human?”
	 We follow the main protagonist Jerome, an AI who deeply admires his creators. He mostly isolates himself away from the other AI, preferring to remain in the abandoned cities of humanity. Jerome feels more connected to humanity, believing a better understanding of them would help his kind, as well as himself, discover their purpose of existing. His hobby; collecting trinkets and mementos of his former creators. In the city he currently resides in, he meets Sonya, an AI like him who separates herself from the other AI to take care of a small group of child bots with her. The child bots are also known as comfort bots since they were made to help humanity cope after children were no longer being born.
Jerome acts on his urge to have a deep conversation with Sonya of what it means to be “alive” as an AI, introducing us to two ways the AI may think about their existence. As Jerome later thinks about this discussion, an alien ship from outer space crashes into his tiny hill, sending all his belongings and himself flying into the air. The alien reveals itself to Jerome, taking particular interest in him. The alien, being part of a species that influences its own evolution, takes interest in both the AI and the humans who made them. The alien asks for a better understanding of them both, to which Jerome decides to explore the abandoned human cities with the alien. After this initial exploration, the alien emphasizes that they want to see the progression of Jerome’s kind. To the reluctance of Jerome, they go on to explore the expanding cities of the AI. Leaving the comfort of the past, it is time for Jerome to confront the future that he has hidden himself away from for so long.
This is the beginning of Jerome, one of the living remnants of humanity, one of the key figures in the AI evolution, one of them, one of us.
